raw:
I ran no new experiments. These ten hypotheses come from the 100 measurements above plus general training behaviour, so the weaker ones are guesses.

- **Strongest evidence:** a high learning rate (0.0215 and above) tends to be unstable. Stepping the learning rate up there crashed accuracy in experiments 3, 10 and 17, and stepping it down gave large gains in experiments 9 and 18. The same instability should make added depth or width hurt at a high learning rate.
- **Alpha:** a high alpha (0.0167 and above) over-regularizes. Raising it cost accuracy in experiments 82, 84 and 97, and lowering it helped in experiments 87 and 93.
- **Weakest:** the batch-size hypothesis rests on a handful of noisy, mixed results (experiments 61, 66 and 70). The low-learning-rate hypotheses lean mostly on the training budget being too short (243 epochs), with little direct evidence.
